errors.what: Foot path is not the characteristic Jansen shape. The flat, straight section of the traced path is a near-vertical edge on the left (x about -117 mm, around crank 150-210 deg) rather than a flat bottom, so the path looks rotated about 90 degrees. The y range (about -91 to +90 mm) is also about as large as the x range, whereas Jansen's foot path is wider than tall with a flat bottom.

Foot y spans both positive and negative values and rises to about 90 mm, so the foot lifts far more than the real mechanism does. It does not look like a ground-contact stride, and the leg triangle looks oversized and swings wildly relative to the other links. This points to a wrong assembly configuration or wrong link-length ratios.
